attempts.label: DANDI:001538
attempts.paper_title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons controls levodopa-induced dyskinesia in a mouse model of Parkinson’s disease

inputs.what: The paper's per-cell and per-mouse tables (Figures 1 to 10 and the supplementary figures), used by the five link claims and by the claims marked data elsewhere.
The paper's somatic excitability script (spike counting and rheobase), read for method details.
The paper's dendritic excitability script (backgrounds, smoothing, windows, basal ratio), read for method details.
The paper's GRAB-ACh3.0 script (F0, AUC window, Fmax and Fmin), read for method details.

attempts.entry_title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons in levodopa-induced dyskinesia (Zhai et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The paper's main findings on striatal neurons held up in this data: on-state dSPNs were more excitable and iSPNs less, at the soma and in dendrites, with M1 receptors and CDGI behind the iSPN dendritic change. Elevated off-state acetylcholine release, the cortical synaptic changes and reduced dyskinesia after iSPN M1 receptor deletion also reproduced. The SCH 23390 reversal in dSPN dendrites held only with one incompletely deposited cell left out (P = 0.027, 0.066 with it). Spine density could not be tested, because the counts used manual steps the paper does not describe. Dyskinesia in CDGI knockouts could not be tested, as the deposited scores differ from the paper's.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Zhai, Cui, Wokosin, Sun, Tkatch, Crittenden, Graybiel and Surmeier (2025) on the draft of dandiset 001538, which holds whole-cell somatic and dendritic excitability recordings of dSPNs and iSPNs in the on- and off-states of levodopa-induced dyskinesia, Sr2+-oEPSC recordings, GRAB-ACh3.0 imaging, AIM score sheets and two-photon spine images. It compares rheobase, spike counts, the dendritic excitability index, Sr2+-oEPSC amplitude and frequency, evoked ACh release and AIM scores between states, drugs and genotypes, and links the files to the paper's per-cell tables.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zhai et al. (2025) from dandiset 001538
Findings of attempt zhai-2025-01 checked on dandiset 001538 version draft

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's somatic current-step recordings are those behind the paper's somatic excitability figures, and the spike counts computed from them agree with the paper's per-cell tables.
outcomes.source: Figures 1E, 3C, 6C, 7C and 9D; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: All 12 groups hold the paper's n (123 cells). Over 20 to 300 pA, 73.2% of cells match a row of the paper's table exactly and 85.4% within 3 spikes in total (criterion 80% and 95%; partial at 50% exact). 97.8% of exact matches fall on the row at the cell's position in date and cell order. Exact matches are lowest in dSPN on-state (40%) and on-state with sulpiride (57%); the largest misses are 20 and 24 spikes. The rheobase equals the first step with a spike in the matched row for 97.8% of exact matches and 87.8% of all cells.
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.
A step recorded twice keeps its first sweep (the paper's script does not say); 14 of 123 cells have a repeated step.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's dendritic line scans are those behind the paper's dendritic excitability index figures, and the index computed from them agrees with the paper's per-cell values.
outcomes.source: Figures 1I, 3F, 6D and 7F; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: The count of cells with an index equals the paper's n in 8 of 10 groups; iSPN on-state (9 against 10) and CDGI KO off-state (10 against 11) each lack a cell imaged at one dendritic site only, at two spots. Over 90 matched cells the index differs from the paper's by a median of 2.8% of its value; 83.7% are within 10%. The Figure 6D identifiers line up with the files' cell numbers (letter c is cell 3), with median differences of 3.5% and 6.4%.
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.
The claims file's 'letter a, b, c for the first, second and third cell of the day' is read as cell number 1, 2, 3; the 6D identifiers include c for days with cells 1 and 3 only.
Rows outside Figure 6D are aligned with every cell that has line scans, in date and cell order, so that a cell without a pair keeps its place.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's Sr2+-oEPSC recordings are cells of the paper's Figures 2 and 4, and their events agree with the paper's per-cell values.
outcomes.source: Figures 2G to 2I and 4F to 4H; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: All 33 dandiset cells match a paper identifier (date and letter, the letter read as cell number) and all 33 paper cells are in the dandiset. At 5 SD the per-cell mean amplitude is within 25% of the paper's for 90.9% of cells, the event count for 42.4%, both for 39.4% (criterion 75%); the detector finds a median 1.33 times the paper's events (1.50 at 4 SD, 2.14 at 3 SD). The paper's per-cell amplitude equals the median of its own event list for all 33 cells, and its event lists hold frequency x 3.6 s events (10 sweeps of 360 ms), while two dandiset cells have 11 and 12 sweeps, all of which are used here. With the per-cell median amplitude, which the paper's tables hold, 66.7% of cells are within 25% on amplitude and 42.4% on both; this attempt asks a reader whether the criterion should compare the median (questions/zhai-2025.yaml). The outcome is partial under either reading.
deviations: Sr2+-oEPSC events come from a stand-in for TaroTools (lid.detect_events), with a 1 ms running mean, the noise SD before the flash, and events whose threshold crossing falls 40 to 400 ms after the flash at more than 5 SD (Methods, Data acquisition and statistical analysis); the smoothing, noise window, local baseline and 3 ms event separation are assumptions, as the paper used TaroTools with visual verification and gives no parameters.
The paper's event count is taken as its frequency times 3.6 s, which equals the length of its event lists.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's GRAB-ACh recordings are regions of the paper's Figure 5F, and the normalised areas computed from them agree with the paper's per-region values.
outcomes.source: Figure 5F; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: The counts per group are the paper's (13 unlesioned, 10 6-OHDA, 11 off-state regions). 16 of 34 dandiset regions match a paper region within 0.05 for every treatment, short of half, and 10 paper regions are the best match of more than one dandiset region; the median of the largest per-treatment difference is 0.052. No identifier links regions, the ROI here is the Methods' 50 um circle on the stored movies where the paper used the region Prairie View saved, and one region takes Fmax from the other region of its slice; these may explain the gaps. The group comparisons of the Figure 5F claims do not use the match. The Methods' Fmin rule, min(TTX, quinpirole), matches best: with TTX only 10 of 33 regions match within 0.05 (the off-state and 6-OHDA medians rise to 0.537 and 0.539, against the paper's 0.36 and 0.306), with the quinpirole baseline only 15 of 34. A one-to-one match (Hungarian assignment within each group) pairs 15 of 34 regions within 0.05 with the Methods' rule and 6 of 33 with TTX only. The outcome is not reproduced under every reading.
deviations: The criterion matches 'each mouse'; this version holds several regions per mouse, so each region, the unit of the paper's table, is matched.

One region (2024-04-02 Slice1Roi2) has no acetylcholine trial; its Fmax is the mean of the other region of its slice, an assumption the paper does not cover. One region (2024-05-24 Slice1Roi1) has no TTX trial; its Fmin is the quinpirole baseline, as the Methods allow.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's AIM score tables are mice of the paper's Figures 8 and 10, with genotypes and scores that agree with the paper's tables.
outcomes.source: Figures 8B, 8C and 10B; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: Figure 8: 18 of the 21 dandiset mice are in the paper's table (4123, 4124 and 5871 are not; 2346, 2347, 7741, 7742 and 7744 of the paper are missing), and their session totals equal the paper's in 6% (control) and 16% (CDGI KO) of sessions, as the dandiset description says. Figure 10: all 21 mice match with their groups and 98% of sessions are equal; mouse 4790 session 3 (44 against 43) and mouse 5845 session 4 (39.5 against 36.5) differ. Genotype labels agree throughout. The link holds for the Figure 10 mice and fails for the Figure 8 mice. No mouse number is in both figures, in the dandiset or in the paper's tables; sessions are matched on figure, mouse and session.
deviations: The session total is the sum over time points of axial, limb and orolingual scores, as the claims file states; the lab's own total column differs from that sum at 5 of 1064 time points.

outcomes.statement: In dSPNs the rheobase is lower in the LID on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2 (P < 0.0001, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: in on-state dSPNs, the current needed to evoke a spike (rheobase) was significantly smaller than that in the off-state
outcomes.notes: Rheobase median 140 pA on-state (15 cells, 10 mice) against 220 pA off-state (15 cells, 8 mice), Mann-Whitney P = 8.9e-06 (paper P < 0.0001). Keeping the last sweep of a repeated step gives the same.
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.

outcomes.statement: In on-state dSPNs suprathreshold current steps evoke more spikes than in off-state dSPNs across a range of intensities.
outcomes.source: Figure 1E; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: the number of spikes evoked by suprathreshold current steps was greater across a range of intensities
outcomes.notes: Spike sum over 20 to 300 pA, median 88 on-state against 36 off-state, P = 8.8e-05; per-step medians higher on-state from 120 pA, P < 0.05 at each step from 100 to 300 pA. 3 on-state and 5 off-state cells miss a step; the mean per step present gives P = 1.4e-04. Keeping the last sweep of a repeated step gives P = 8.8e-05.
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.

outcomes.statement: Bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390 does not reverse the lower rheobase of on-state dSPNs.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2 (P = 0.589, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390 (3 μM) did not reverse the leftward shift in the F-I relationship curve (Fig. 1E) or the reduction in rheobase
outcomes.notes: Rheobase median 140 pA on-state (15 cells) and 140 pA with SCH 23390 (10 cells), P = 1.0 (paper P = 0.589). The 5 cells recorded in both conditions give Wilcoxon P = 1.0. Keeping the last sweep of a repeated step gives P = 1.0.
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.

outcomes.statement: The dendritic excitability index of dSPNs is higher in the on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.source: Figure 1I; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 3 (P = 0.0115, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: the dendritic excitability of dSPNs in the on-state was higher than in the LID off-state
outcomes.notes: Index median 0.476 on-state against 0.353 off-state (10 cells each), P = 0.0091 (paper P = 0.0115). Pairing every proximal with every distal site gives P = 0.017. No pair falls outside the basal-ratio range (0.67 to 1.75).
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.

The index follows the paper's script (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14163502) on the stored line profiles: backgrounds 55 and 161, a 6-sample running mean, trials of a site averaged, R0 and G0 from 0.5 to 0.95 s, the area of dG/R0 from 0.95 to 1.5 s.

outcomes.statement: SCH 23390 reverses the higher dendritic excitability of on-state dSPNs.
outcomes.source: Figure 1I; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 3 (P = 0.0133, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: the elevation in on-state dSPN dendritic excitability was readily reversed by bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390

statistics.n: 10 on-state and 9 on-state with SCH cells

outcomes.notes: Without 2019-04-11 cell 1, whose first site pair the dandiset does not hold (its description, item 3), the SCH 23390 median is 0.384 (8 cells) against 0.476 on-state (10 cells), P = 0.027, and 0.034 pairing every proximal with every distal site, the SCH median lower. With that cell, P = 0.066 (median 0.419, 9 cells) and 0.079. From its second pair alone the cell's index is 0.584, against the paper's 0.228; of the other eight SCH cells, seven are within 10% of the paper's rows and 2019-05-03 cell 3 differs by 10.9% (0.289 against 0.261). On the paper's own table the exact test gives P = 0.0133, the paper's value, and 0.027 without that row. No cell has an index in both conditions; the on-state cells are from 2017 and the SCH cells from 2019.
deviations: Groups come from the files' condition column; the claims file names a condition_subfolder column, which this version of the dandiset does not have.

Assumption: 2019-04-11 cell 1 is left out of the SCH 23390 group. The dandiset holds only the second of its two proximal-distal site pairs (description, item 3), so its index cannot be computed as the paper computed it; with it the test gives P = 0.066 and the claim would not be reproduced.

outcomes.statement: dSPN somatic excitability (rheobase) rises after the 6-OHDA lesion and falls in the LID off-state.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2 (both P < 0.0001)
outcomes.quote: somatic excitability of dSPNs was significantly increased following 6-OHDA lesioning and decreased by repetitive doses of levodopa when assessed in the off-state
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table: dSPN rheobase median 120 pA after 6-OHDA against 220 pA in controls (P = 0.00030), and 200 pA off-state against 120 pA (P = 9.5e-05).
outcomes.where: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059 (per-cell rheobase, Figure 1F sheet); raw recordings in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198

outcomes.statement: The dSPN dendritic excitability index is not changed by the 6-OHDA lesion or in the off-state.
outcomes.source: Figure 1I; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 3 (P = 0.824 and 0.905)
outcomes.quote: This index of dendritic excitability was not significantly different in dSPNs from 6-OHDA–lesioned mice or LID mice in the off-state
outcomes.notes: On the paper's table: control against 6-OHDA P = 0.82, 6-OHDA against off-state P = 0.90 (paper 0.824 and 0.905).

outcomes.statement: The amplitude of Sr2+-oEPSCs evoked from cortical afferents is larger in on-state than in off-state dSPNs.
outcomes.source: Figures 2G and 2H (P = 0.0003, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: the Sr2+-oEPSC amplitude was significantly larger in on-state dSPNs than in off-state dSPNs
outcomes.notes: At 5 SD the per-cell median amplitude, the adopted reading, is a median 12.5 pA on-state (8 cells, 4 mice) against 8.4 pA off-state (10 cells, 3 subjects), P = 0.0044 (paper P = 0.0003); the per-cell mean gives 15.6 against 10.1 pA, P = 0.0031. Of the six readings (3, 4 and 5 SD; mean or median) five give P < 0.05 with the on-state larger; 3 SD with the median gives P = 0.068. Open for the paper's authors: the TaroTools settings (filtering, how the noise SD was measured, baseline and event separation) and whether events were removed at visual verification; the detector here finds a median 1.33 times the paper's events at 5 SD. On the paper's own per-cell amplitudes the test gives P = 0.0003 with the on-state larger.
deviations: Sr2+-oEPSC events come from a stand-in for TaroTools (lid.detect_events), with a 1 ms running mean, the noise SD before the flash, and events whose threshold crossing falls 40 to 400 ms after the flash at more than 5 SD (Methods, Data acquisition and statistical analysis); the smoothing, noise window, local baseline and 3 ms event separation are assumptions, as the paper used TaroTools with visual verification and gives no parameters.
The reading the paper best supports is adopted: 5 SD (Methods) and the per-cell median, which the paper's table holds; the per-cell mean is shown too and gives the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: The frequency of Sr2+-oEPSCs in dSPNs does not differ between states.
outcomes.source: Figure 2I (P = 0.127)
outcomes.quote: Although the frequency of on-state Sr2+-oEPSCs trended toward higher values (Fig. 2I), as did spine density (Fig. 2, B and C), the differences between states were not statistically significant
outcomes.notes: Frequency median 28.6 Hz on-state against 23.1 Hz off-state at 5 SD, P = 0.122 (paper P = 0.127); 4 and 3 SD give P = 0.0505 and 0.068. The detector finds more events than the paper (median 1.33 times), so absolute frequencies are higher than the paper's. Open for the paper's authors: the TaroTools settings (filtering, how the noise SD was measured, baseline and event separation) and whether events were removed at visual verification; the detector here finds a median 1.33 times the paper's events at 5 SD. On the paper's own per-cell frequencies the test gives P = 0.130 (exact 0.146), 20.1 Hz on-state against 16.5 Hz, so the absence holds on the paper's values too; the detector's 4 SD reading (P = 0.0505) is the thinnest margin.
deviations: Sr2+-oEPSC events come from a stand-in for TaroTools (lid.detect_events), with a 1 ms running mean, the noise SD before the flash, and events whose threshold crossing falls 40 to 400 ms after the flash at more than 5 SD (Methods, Data acquisition and statistical analysis); the smoothing, noise window, local baseline and 3 ms event separation are assumptions, as the paper used TaroTools with visual verification and gives no parameters.

outcomes.statement: dSPN spine density falls in the off-state, and mushroom spines are more common in the on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.source: Figures 2A to 2C
outcomes.quote: in dSPNs taken from LID mice that were in the off-state, spine density in both dendritic regions was significantly reduced ... in the on-state, enlarged, mushroom spines were more common in both distal and proximal dendrites

statistics.about: off-state spine density reduction, proximal dendrites
off-state spine density reduction, distal dendrites
mushroom spines, on-state against off-state, distal dendrites
mushroom spines, on-state against off-state, proximal dendrites

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 76 two-photon spine Z-stack files (Figures 2, 4, 6, 7 and 9) but no spine counts, and its description says the rows of the paper's spine tables cannot be matched to the files. The paper deconvolved the stacks in AutoQuant X3.0.4 and counted spines semi-automatically in NeuronStudio with manual correction (Methods, Imaging of spines and dendritic Ca2+ transients); the manual steps are not described, so no automatic count has a basis in the paper. Not attempted.

outcomes.statement: Confocal spine density of iSPN proximal dendrites is higher than the 2PLSM estimate (median 2.084 against 1.243 spines per um), falls after the lesion, rises modestly in the off-state and falls in the on-state.

findings.statement: Two cells with dendritic line scans were imaged at one dendritic site only, at two spots: 2016-05-26 cell 3 (CDGI knockout, off-state, Distal1 Spot1 and Spot2) and 2016-06-08 cell 1 (on-state, Proximal1 Spot1 and Spot2). They have no proximal-distal pair and no index, while the paper counts them in Figures 3F and 7F (10 and 11 cells).

The first proximal-distal site pair of dSPN 2019-04-11 cell 1 (on-state with SCH 23390, Figure 1I) is not deposited, as the dandiset description says. From its second pair alone the cell's index is 0.584, against the paper's 0.228, and the Figure 1I comparison of on-state with SCH 23390 gives P = 0.066 with the cell and 0.027 without it (paper 0.0133).

The somatic spike counts of 33 of 123 cells, computed from the files with the paper's rule (upward crossings of 0 mV), do not equal any row of the paper's per-cell table over 20 to 300 pA; 18 differ by more than 3 spikes, up to 24. Exact agreement is lowest in dSPN on-state (6 of 15) and iSPN on-state with sulpiride (4 of 7).

The AIM sheets of the Figure 8 mice differ from the paper's table in most sessions (session totals equal in 6% of control and 16% of CDGI knockout sessions), mice 4123, 4124 and 5871 are not in the paper, and 7741, 7742, 7744, 2346 and 2347 of the paper are missing, as the dandiset description states. The Figure 10 sheets match the paper in 103 of 105 sessions.
Mouse 7830 (Figure 10, control) has identical AIM sheets for sessions 4 and 5; the paper's table has the same values for both sessions.

Subjects are defined per recording day. Mouse counts differ from the paper's legends in four groups (Sr2+-oEPSC dSPN and iSPN off-state, 3 subjects against 4 mice; M1R CRISPR control and deletion somatic cells, 2 and 3 against 3 and 4), which mice sharing a recording day would explain; the files do not say which mouse each cell came from.

The GRAB-ACh3.0 regions and the paper's ROIs share no identifier, so the per-region areas cannot be linked one by one; matching by values pairs 16 of 34 regions within 0.05. One region (2024-04-02 Slice1Roi2) has no acetylcholine trial for Fmax and one (2024-05-24 Slice1Roi1) has no TTX trial.

Two Sr2+-oEPSC cells hold more sweeps than the paper's frequencies imply (2023-02-22 cell 1, 12 sweeps; 2023-04-06 cell 1, 11 sweeps; the paper's event lists equal frequency x 10 sweeps of 360 ms), and the files do not say which sweeps the paper used.

The control and 6-OHDA patch-clamp recordings of Figures 1 and 3, the rotation counts and the open-field data are not in the dandiset, as its description says; the claims on them can be tested only on the paper's tables.

The session names of the SCH 23390 and sulpiride files (D1RaSch, D2RaSul) state a drug, while 11 somatic cells in these files have baseline on-state sweeps and 4 of them are baseline only (dSPN 2019-05-07 cell 1, iSPN 2019-04-08 cell 1, 2019-04-09 cell 1 and 2019-05-08 cell 2). Each sweep's group is in the condition and drug columns of the intracellular recordings table; grouping by session name puts these cells in the drug groups.

18 of 123 somatic cells have no sweep at one or more current steps between 20 and 300 pA, and 14 of these have another step recorded twice (dSPN 2017-07-07 cell 2, on-state, has none at 100 and at 220 to 300 pA and two at -20 pA). Their spike counts over 20 to 300 pA cannot be complete.

paper_notes.statement: The per-cell Sr2+-oEPSC amplitudes of Figures 2H and 4G, labelled average amplitude in the paper's tables, equal the median of each cell's event list in the Figure 2G and 4F sheets for all 33 cells and the mean for none.

The Sr2+-oEPSC events were detected with TaroTools in Igor Pro, followed by visual verification, with a threshold of five SD above the noise; the paper gives no filter, noise window, baseline or event separation, and does not say whether events were removed at verification. Which settings were used? A stand-in detector finds a median 1.33 times the paper's events at 5 SD, though the state comparisons agree.

Spine densities (Figures 2, 4, 6, 7 and 9 from two-photon stacks; Figure 4K from confocal stacks) were counted in NeuronStudio and in Imaris with manual correction, and the dandiset holds the images but no counts. What did the manual correction change (spines added or removed, by what rule), and could the counts per dendrite, with the file and segment each comes from, be deposited with the images?

Recomputed on the paper's per-cell tables (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059), two reported P values differ. The Wilcoxon test of oxo-M in CDGI KO iSPNs (Figure 7E, 12 cells) gives P = 0.4697 where the paper reports 0.910, and the Mann-Whitney test of rotations in Figure 8A (10 KO and 12 wild-type mice) gives P = 0.01198 where the paper reports 0.0092. The wild-type oxo-M test gives P = 0.009766, as the paper's 0.0098.

entries.name: zhai-2025
entries.title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons in levodopa-induced dyskinesia (Zhai et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zhai, Cui, Wokosin, Sun, Tkatch, Crittenden, Graybiel and Surmeier (2025) on the draft of dandiset 001538, which holds whole-cell somatic and dendritic excitability recordings of dSPNs and iSPNs in the on- and off-states of levodopa-induced dyskinesia, Sr2+-oEPSC recordings, GRAB-ACh3.0 imaging, AIM score sheets and two-photon spine images. It compares rheobase, spike counts, the dendritic excitability index, Sr2+-oEPSC amplitude and frequency, evoked ACh release and AIM scores between states, drugs and genotypes, and links the files to the paper's per-cell tables.
